A distinguishable part of a sequence or cycle occurring over time.
That which is exhibited to the eye; the appearance which anything manifests, especially any one among different and varying appearances of the same object.
Any appearance or aspect of an object of mental apprehension or view.

examples.text: The problem has many phases.

glosses: A particular appearance or state in a regularly recurring cycle of changes with respect to quantity of illumination or form, or the absence, of a body's illuminated disk. Illustrated in Wikipedia's article Lunar phase.

examples.text: the phases of the moon

glosses: Any one point or portion in a recurring series of changes, as in the changes of motion of one of the particles constituting a wave or vibration; one portion of a series of such changes, in distinction from a contrasted portion, as the portion on one side of a position of equilibrium, in contrast with that on the opposite side.

A component in a material system that is distinguished by chemical composition and/or physical state (solid, liquid or gas) and/or crystal structure. It is delineated from an adjoining phase by an abrupt change in one or more of those conditions.
In certain organisms, one of two or more colour variations characteristic of the species, but independent of the ordinary seasonal and sexual differences, and often also of age.
The period of play between consecutive breakdowns.

examples.text: When Romania did manage to string together some phases midway through the first half, England's discipline held firm, although on the whole it was a less focused display from the Six Nations champions in the second half.

glosses: A haplotype.

The counterclockwise angle from the positive half of the real number line to the vector pointing to a complex number on an Argand diagram of the complex plane, which has the positive real line pointing right and the positive imaginary number line pointing up.
A distortion caused by a difference in the speed of propagation for different frequencies
In a polyphase electrical power system, one of the power-carrying conductors, or the alternating current carried by it.
To begin—if construed with \"in\"—or to discontinue—if construed with out—(doing) something over a period of time (i.e. in phases).

examples.text: The use of the obsolete machines was gradually phased out as the new models were phased in.

glosses: To determine haplotypes in (data) when genotypes are known.
To pass into or through a solid object.

examples.text: Anyone who has lost their way in cyberspace—realizing they have just phased into what they had previously categorized as 'solid' matter—will understand this example.
Archer took a deep breath and, steeling himself for the bizarre experience, carefully walked to the bulkhead and phased through.

To be alive; to have life.

examples.text: He's not expected to live for more than a few months.

glosses: To have permanent residence somewhere, to inhabit, to reside.

examples.text: I live at 2a Acacia Avenue.  At that time I'd been living in a camper for about six months.

The young priests who lived here wore cassocks and birettas; their faces were fine and mild, yet really strong, like the rector's face; and in their intercourse with him and his wife they seemed to be brothers.

glosses: To have permanent residence somewhere, to inhabit, to reside.
(of an object) to have its proper place; to normally be stored.

examples.text: I washed your gravy boat. Where does it live?

glosses: To survive; to persevere; to continue.

examples.text:
When Lazarus left his charnel-cave,
⁠And home to Mary’s house return’d, […]
‘Where wert thou, brother, those four days?’
⁠There lives no record of reply,
⁠Which telling what it is to die
Had surely added praise to praise.

glosses: To endure in memory; to escape oblivion.

examples.text: Her memory lives in that song.

He has now overseen three straight victories since taking over from Claudio Ranieri and this latest win, against one of the best teams in Europe, will live long in the memory for every Leicester supporter.

glosses: To cope.

examples.text: You'll just have to live with it!  I can't live in a world without you.

glosses: To pass life in a specified manner.

examples.text: It is difficult to live in poverty.   And they lived happily ever after.

glosses: To spend, as one's life; to pass; to maintain; to continue in, constantly or habitually.

examples.text: To live an idle or a useful life.
Many people write their romances, others live them; Honore de Balzac did both.

His son was regarded as a shadowy playboy, with rumours circulating over the years that he imported Russian and Chinese prostitutes, and lived a life of profligacy and excess.

examples.text: to live the Gospel

glosses: To outlast danger; (of a ship or boat) to float.

examples.text: That rockslide trapped me in a cave, and I was trapped for three days, but I lived.
No ship could live in such a storm.
a strong mast that lived upon the sea

glosses: To maintain or support one's existence; to provide for oneself; to feed; to subsist.

examples.text: It is hard to live on the minimum wage.   They lived on stale bread.   Man shall not live by bread alone.

glosses: To make the most of life; to experience a full, rich life.

examples.text: I'm sick of spending every day studying at home: I want to go out there and live!

glosses: Having life; that is alive.

examples.text: The post office will not ship live animals.

glosses: Being in existence; actual.

examples.text: He is a live example of the consequences of excessive drinking.

glosses: Having active properties; being energized.

examples.text: Because the vaccinia virus is live, it is important to follow care instructions for the vaccination site.

glosses: Operational; in actual use rather than in testing etc.

Of an object or value: that may potentially be used in the future execution of a program.

examples.text: An object in the heap is live if its address is held in a root, or there is a pointer to it held in another live heap node.

glosses: Taken from a living animal.

examples.text: live feathers

glosses: Imparting power; having motion.

examples.text: the live spindle of a lathe
a live, or driving, axle

glosses: Still in active play.

examples.text: a live ball

glosses: Of a card: not yet dealt or played.

examples.text: As a beginner, when you are in a hand, you should practice counting your outs, or those live cards left in the deck that can improve your hand.

glosses: Being broadcast (\"on the air\"), as it happens.

examples.text: The station presented a live news program every evening.
Are we live?

glosses: In person.

examples.text: This nightclub has a live band on weekends.

glosses: Recorded from a performance in front of an audience.

examples.text: a live album

glosses: Able to fire or explode (of firearms or explosives).

examples.text: The air force practices dropping live bombs on the uninhabited island.

glosses: Of an environment where sound is recorded: having noticeable reverberation.

examples.text: A good experiment is to have a friend stand in a fixed position in a moderately live room and talk in a clear voice.
It sounds like the instruments were recorded in a fairly live room with reverb added.

glosses: Electrically charged or energized, usually indicating that the item may cause electrocution if touched.

examples.text: Use caution when working near live wires.

glosses: Being a bet which can be raised by the bettor, usually in reference to a blind or straddle.

examples.text: Tommy's blind was live, so he was given the option to raise.

glosses: Featuring humans; not animated, in the phrases “live actors” or “live action”.
Being in a state of ignition; burning.

examples.text: a live coal; live embers

glosses: Vivid; bright.

examples.text: the live carnation

glosses: Energetic, attentive, active.

examples.text: a live man, or orator

glosses: Outstanding, top-notch, exhilarating.

examples.text: The party was live, and the music was jammin. All over the beach people in colorful swimsuits were moving to the beat.

glosses: Of a syllable in languages such as Thai and Burmese: resonating, not ending abruptly.
Of an event, as it happens; in real time; direct.

examples.text: The concert was broadcast live by radio.

glosses: Of making a performance or speech, in person.

examples.text: He'll be appearing live at the auditorium.
